chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to me from al-Hasan ibn Ishaq al-Tajir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from one who narrated it from al-Harith ibn al-Ahwal, the companion of al-Taqq, from Jamil ibn Salih, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Do not be deceived by people regarding yourself,
for the matter will reach you from them [or: without them]. Do not pass the day with 'such and such', for with you is one who records [your deeds] upon you.
And I have never seen anything that is more intense in pursuit and faster in attainment than a good deed for an old sin.
And do not consider small any good deed, for you will see it tomorrow in a place that pleases you.
And do not consider small any evil deed, for you will see it tomorrow in a place that displeases you.
Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Surely good deeds wipe out sins.'
This is a reminder for those who remember.
ai.seo_question: How do good deeds affect old sins according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) encourages believers to maintain spiritual vigilance by recognizing that divine accountability is direct and not mediated by public opinion. He emphasizes the transformative power of consistent good deeds to erase past sins, warning against underestimating the cumulative impact of even small acts of virtue or vice. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of *hasana* (good deed) as a means of spiritual purification and readiness for the Hereafter.
